cards.title: Missed a dose? Don't panic
cards.body: It happens to everyone, especially parents juggling several strips. A calm, safe response matters more than a quick one.

cards.title: Don't double up
cards.body: Taking two doses to catch up can cause problems. Don't double the next dose unless a doctor or pharmacist tells you to.

cards.title: Check the leaflet
cards.body: Many medicine boxes come with a leaflet that says what to do if a dose is missed. Read that part first.

cards.title: Ask the pharmacist
cards.body: Call your chemist with the medicine name, the usual timing and when it was missed. They can tell you what to do for that medicine.

cards.title: Some medicines need a quicker call
cards.body: For insulin, blood thinners, seizure or heart medicines, check with the doctor or pharmacist promptly rather than guessing.

cards.title: Make it less likely next time
cards.body: A pill organiser, a reminder at the same time every day, or linking the dose to a meal. Small systems beat willpower.

cards.title: Calm, check, ask
cards.body: Don't double, read the leaflet, ask the pharmacist. If they feel unwell in a worrying way, get medical help.

takeaway: If a dose is missed, don't double up. Check the leaflet or ask your pharmacist what to do for that medicine.
share: Save this for the next "arre, subah wali goli reh gayi" moment.
